links.targetTitle: An Integration Boost payment found inaccurate by Core GovOps
Every reward payment records its transaction hash and amount

title: The Atlas specifies how Core GovOps flags an inaccurate reward payment but leaves the consequence marked TBD
content:
A.2.2.9.1.2.4.1.3.3 gives Core GovOps two mutually exclusive pathways at quarterly review. The confirmation pathway sets Confirmation to Yes with optional commentary and triggers the Sky Core Atlas update that begins reimbursement. The rejection pathway sets Confirmation to No with **required** commentary and triggers "Payment Inaccuracy Previously Found By Core GovOps."

That trigger target is then left blank. A.2.2.9.1.2.4.1.3.4.1 lists the outputs for both branches and, under "Payment Inaccuracy Previously Found By Core GovOps," states simply: **TBD**.

So the settlement chain's only verification gate has a fully specified pass path and an unspecified fail path. Detection is defined; remedy is not. What happens to the already-disbursed funds, whether the Executor's reimbursement is withheld or partially paid, and how the figure is corrected are all outside the Process Definition.

Some of the substance exists elsewhere — A.2.2.9.1.2.1.3.4 requires the Prime Agent to reimburse overpayments and allows it to recoup from future rewards — but that provision addresses the Prime, while the party out of pocket at this point in the chain is the Operational Executor Agent whose Buffer funded the payment. The TBD sits exactly where those two facts need to be reconciled.

Worth recording because the gap is structural rather than cosmetic: the pay-first-verify-later design (A.2.2.9.1.2.4.1) depends entirely on the failure branch working, and that branch is the one not yet written.
description: The rejection pathway requires written reasoning and names a follow-on output that is unspecified, so the only detection gate in the settlement chain has no defined remedy.
